title: Policy-driven undo layer: snapshots + traffic simulation for safe config changes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Goal:
Build an explicit undo layer for runtime configuration changes that combines atomic state snapshots, traffic replay simulation, and policy-driven automatic rollback triggers. This will let us safely apply complex cost optimization recommendations (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization toggles) and automatically revert changes when regressions or cost/latency degradations are detected.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: Config changes (batching parameters, cache TTLs, kernel-selection toggles) can yield large cost wins but occasionally introduce regressions in latency, error rates, or output quality. Current ad-hoc rollback tooling and human-run playbooks are slow and brittle for high-velocity config tuning.
- Outcome: A deterministic undo flow that: 1) captures a consistent snapshot of all config state before apply; 2) runs a fast traffic-sim preflight against a shadow environment using recent request distributions; 3) applies canary and monitors safety signals; 4) triggers automated rollback when defined thresholds are crossed; 5) reconciles state if partial failures occur.

Design highlights:
1) Snapshot store: before any change, persist a versioned snapshot containing the full config diff (service-level batching parameters, cache profiles, quantization flags, routing policies) and metadata (who, why, timestamp). Snapshots are immutable and referenced by a UUID. Retention: 30 days by default; configurable per project.
2) Flight simulator: lightweight request replay harness that samples 5–10k recent anonymized requests from the request-events stream and replays them against the canary runtime in shadow mode. Collects latency percentiles, token throughput, error rates, and cost-per-token estimates (using an internal microcost model).
3) Policy engine: declarative rules shipped with every change (example: rollback if P95 latency increases > 25ms AND error-rate increase > 0.5%, OR cost-per-token increases > 20% without quality improvement). Policies support hard thresholds and relative-percentile guards.
4) Apply model: staged apply: (a) preflight (snapshot + flight sim dry-run), (b) small canary (1% traffic) with metric-based quick-eval window (2–5 minutes), (c) ramp to target with hysteresis and cooldowns.
5) Automatic rollback: triggers can be metric-based (SLO violations, cost regressions), anomaly-based (statistical divergence using EWMA + MAD), or manual. Rollback runs a fast restore using the referenced snapshot and validates reconciliation across control plane and serving nodes.
6) Reconciliation: if some nodes never received the rollback (network partitions, async apply), a reconciliation job walks the fleet, compares live config hashes to the snapshot hash, and repairs drift. All actions are idempotent.

Telemetry and observability:
- Per-change timeline in Console: preflight summary, flight-sim results, canary metrics, rollback decision and snapshot UUIDs.
- Auto-generated post-mortem attachments for every rollback with links to PRs, diffs, and metric graphs.
- Cost impact estimates surfaced before final ramp (expected savings and worst-case delta).

Acceptance criteria:
- Preflight snapshot + flight-sim runs for any config change created via Console API or CLI.
- Policy engine enforces at least three baseline guards (latency, error-rate, cost).
- Automatic rollback can restore snapshot in <45s for fleets up to 200 nodes in staging.
- Reconciliation job completes full fleet repair within 10 minutes for 95% of simulated partitions.
- Console shows end-to-end timeline and links to artifacts for every applied change.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Snapshot backend: etcd vs dedicated blob store (we currently prototype with S3 + index service; S3 gives larger retention and simpler snapshots but slower immediate read for restore).
- Flight-sim fidelity vs speed: initial target is 10k replayed requests for fast preflight (~30–90s) vs longer full fidelity runs.
- Tightness of default thresholds: conservative defaults reduce false positive rollbacks but slow innovation. We propose opt-in aggressive profiles for RapidCost experiments.

Next milestones:
- Week 1: complete snapshot schema + API and hook into config apply flow (Aisha, Miguel).
- Week 2: implement flight-sim harness and integrate with anonymized request sampling (Jordan).
- Week 3: policy engine MVP + basic console views (Miguel, SRE).
- Week 4: canary execution path + auto-rollback implementation and reconciliation job (Engineering).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha in testbeds only (internal infra) for 2 weeks.
2) Beta for chosen customers (cost-optimization partners) with manual approval.
3) General availability as runtime-1.20 with docs and playbooks.

Security and privacy:
- Replayed request payloads are anonymized and sampled; PII filters applied.
- Snapshots do NOT store customer prompt content, only config and metric references.

- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Undo+Layer+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2821
- Flight-sim prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/flight/flight-sim-proto

Policy engine enforces latency, error-rate, and cost guards by default
Automated rollback restores snapshot in <45s in staging up to 200 nodes
Reconciliation job repairs 95% of simulated partitioned nodes within 10 minutes
Console timeline shows preflight, canary, and rollback artifacts for each change
comments: 2026-03-04 - Aisha: Initial draft and design review requested. Attached prototype PR in runtime repo.
2026-03-05 - Jordan Lee (SRE): Flight-sim needs throttling logic to avoid amplifying spikes when replaying; will add rate control and synthetic backpressure emulation.
2026-03-07 - Product (Nora Patel): Default policy thresholds should be conservative for GA. Add 'aggressive' profile flag for experiments and opt-in customers.
2026-03-10 - Miguel: Snapshot restore demo successful in staging for a 50-node pool (restore time avg 28s). Filing follow-up task to optimize S3 object fetch parallelism.
2026-03-12 - Security (Elena Grayson): Confirmed snapshots do not include prompt content; recommend encryption-at-rest for snapshot blobs and KMS integration (tracking ENG-13602).
2026-03-14 - Miguel: Implemented canary metric hooks and basic policy checks. Next: reconcile worker for partial-failure scenarios. Planning to open PR by EOD 2026-03-16.
